findings.text: Node B1's block names no existing test for the committed-plan requirement the node's done-when lists, though eight such tests exist at HEAD (tests/test_crew.py:1233, :1255, :1272, :1342, :2343, :4097, :4152, :4209 plus tests/test_skill_contracts.py:1126), so a dispatcher for B1 cannot see what pins the refusal the brief path must bypass.

the verification paragraph states every path:line citation was extracted and checked, but the extractor's regex admits only .py/.toml/.lock/.json/.html, leaving the 6 .md citations and 64 abbreviated continuations unextracted; they all resolve at 2c5a4fee today, yet the sentence claims a coverage the pass does not have.

the control log's rows read "FAIL reckon/crew/recovery.py:999999" without the reason column verify-citations.sh actually prints, so the rows are typed rather than captured output; the discrimination they assert is real (I reproduced 2 FAIL rows through the unmodified script), but the delivered log cannot show the pipeline produced them.

item_verdicts.diff: there are no commits (commits: []), so the landed change is the five artefacts at the reports path, read individually against the reviewed revision 2c5a4fee.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when asks for reuse candidates with file:line at HEAD, derived write files, existing demotion and committed-plan tests, live claims, and every citation resolving; the citation half is asserted by verify-citations.sh and reproduced byte-identically at 85 OK / 0 FAIL, and the test-inventory half is not measured by any gate.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is a reuse map for the four S24 plans naming the existing code each implementable section extends; reuse-map.md:22-249 delivers all twelve sections with file:line reuse candidates, per-node derived write scopes and a live-claims table, and every citation I resolved independently holds, but the test inventory the done-when also asks for covers only one of its two categories (see FINDING reuse-map.md:102).
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits empty with the deliverable outside the repository, the citation tally recorded, and the red log named at control.log — but that log is typed rather than captured (see FINDING control.log:3).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared scope is the reports directory /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/s23-coord/s24-reuse-map; the five landed artefacts (reuse-map.md, verify-citations.sh, citations.tsv, citation-check.log, control.log) are all inside it and the reviewed worktree is clean at 2c5a4fee.

justifications.durability: verify-citations.sh is a real guard that reddens on a broken citation — I reproduced its 2 FAIL rows by appending bogus citations to a copy — but its extractor has the same blind spot, so a regression in any of the 70 abbreviated or .md citations leaves the guard green.
justifications.evidence: verify-citations.sh resolves the map's citations at 2c5a4fee and I reproduced citations.tsv byte-identically (85 OK, 0 FAIL) with a red control of 2 FAIL rows through the unmodified script, but its extractor covers only .py/.toml/.lock/.json/.html, so the 6 .md citations and 64 abbreviated continuations (70 instances, all verified by me to hold) sit outside the tally the map claims is complete at reuse-map.md:269.
justifications.fit: the report follows the store's artefact idiom (markdown plus a runnable checker and its logs, no version suffixes or plan labels in filenames), and its citations use the file:line form the surrounding reports use.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reuse-map.md:22-249 maps every section of the four plans with reuse candidates whose cited lines carry the named symbols (e.g. reckon/crew/recovery.py:3066 define classify_pointer), but the committed-plan test inventory required by the same done-when is absent from reuse-map.md:102-115.
justifications.scope_discipline: all five artefacts are inside the declared fence directory and git status in the reviewed worktree at 2c5a4fee is empty, so the read-only investigation changed no repository path.
